newsitem.title: INDIA: British investment in India seen growing sharply.
newsitem.headline: British investment in India seen growing sharply.

text.p: British investment and trade in India are expected to grow sharply following recent initiatives linked to India's economic reform programme, Indian industry leaders said on Wednesday.

J.J. Irani, co-chairman of a bilateral business institution, Indo-British Partnership, told a news conference in Calcutta that Britain was one of the biggest foreign investors in India, with a cumulative investment figure of three billion pounds.

The investment is targeted to grow to five billion pounds by 2000, Irani said ahead of a three-day business conference organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), India's premier industry association.
British Prime Minister John Major and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda are scheduled to attend the conference, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of India's independence from Britain in 1947.
Major will be accompanied by a 100-strong business delegation.
Britain stepped up its interest in India after New Delhi launched a free-market economic reform programme in 1991. The Indo-British Partnership was founded two years ago.
CII president Shekhar Datta said bilateral trade, which was worth three billion pounds in 1996 is expected to grow to five billion pounds by 2000, the same amount as expected investment.
"We expect that the coming three days will receive a further boost in relationship," Irani said.

Irani identified infrastructure, education, financial services, trading, tourism, mining and manufacturing as key areas in which there was scope for enhanced business relations between India and Britain.

CII officials said the British business community in India had doubled over the past five years and the number of business visits from Britain grew five-fold in the past three years. They could not provide details immediately.
